productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Overall, I really like this watch and do recommend this smartwatch for Samsung Galaxy smartphone users.  This device works well with my Samsung Galaxy A54 5G smartphone.  I use this watch in conjunction with my smartphone, Samsung Health and the Sleepasandroid app.  I basically wanted a full fledged smartwatch that doubled as a health tracker.  This watch fits that purpose really well.  I can keep track of most things on my watch without having to pull out my phone.  I can also take phone calls, send quick responses to text messages and use google pay.  As I mentioned earlier, between Samsung Health and my Sleepasandroid app, I am able to track and try to improve my health.  The only real downside to this watch is the battery life.  Since I like to use this device as a sleep tracker and told Sleepasandroid to use this watch for sleep tracking, it takes a little more battery.  My watch is typically around 45% power about 24 hours later.  So technically, I probably could use this a day and a half before charging it again.  However, I don't want to take any chances of it dying, so I charge it daily.  I typically either charge it around dinner time, or when I get my shower for the day.  With both methods I just let it charge until it is done.(I want to make sure it has plenty of power for sleep tracking.)  The smartwatch sends a notification to your phone once it is done charging.  This watch is really nice for Samsung Galaxy smartphone users.  However, if you want more battery life, you might be better off to go with the Samsung Galaxy 7 Ultra instead.(Has a bigger battery and lasts longer)  Other than the poor battery life, I love this watch.  I just make sure I charge it once daily, so it doesn't die on me.

Unfortunately it's well past the return window.This Apple Watch was supposed to come with LTE. It connected to the cellular network but could only connect via data. It could not make calls when on the cellular network. I kept blaming the wireless carrier assuming that's where the issue was. Afterall, the watch was able to connect to the cellular network.I activated another watch (not bought at Amazon) with the same wireless carrier and everything worked seamlessly including making calls on the cellular network. That's when I realized that I was sold a non-performing unit.You can't trust this buyer to have fully tested the the watch. You apparently need to be a technical expert and test the watch thoroughly within the return window. This is not what I was expecting from this company as a lay consumer. Not a great experience and I'm never going to buy anything from them. I hope Amazon will do something about this company too.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Had this watch for about a week now. I was initially hesitant about the purchase, as this is my first smart watch. After research, and getting acquainted with the tool, I'm so happy I pulled the trigger. I use it every day for surprisingly detailed sleep tracking, enhanced step/activity tracking, ease of checking notifications and responding when I don't have easy access to my phone (or if I'm not supposed to at work), and on top of all of that, it's just a fantastic looking watch. The amount of functions you have access to is fantastic. I have paid more in my life for a watch that literally could only tell time. Lol. I know the health monitoring data may not be spot on, but it has really helped me focus on the right things during day to day. If you're on the fence, do it. If you have a Samsung phone, definitely do it.Some tips:1.) I recommend the first thing you do is order the official Samsung wireless charger to go with it. The charger shipped with this watch is off-brand and charges at about 5 watts, which takes about 2.5-3 hours. The Samsung charger provides 10 watt fast charging which takes 90 minutes at most. Again, the included charger is aftermarket, and slooowww. Get the Samsung one. The battery life on this watch is good, but not phenomenal, so having a faster charger is key to low stress ownership. These smart devices take at least one or two charge cycles to optimize battery use, so be patient with the first couple of battery cycles. I got one day out of the first two, then started getting a full 2 days easy, with slight tweaks to functions, but still fairly liberal use. I've attached screen shots of my batter usage stats after the break in period. If you want to have everything running all day at full capacity, again definitely get the Samsung charger so you can juice up faster after a day of heavy use.2.) This is not a brand new watch. It was manufactured in 2022, and used by a previous owner for years. Do not expect it to be in perfect cosmetic condition. For the price, I think this is reasonable (approx $100 vs $400 new when it came out). Mine has a couple of blemishes, but the screen is in excellent condition. Still looks great to my eye! Consider getting a case and screen protector.3.) I also recommend taking some rubbing alcohol, a micro fiber cloth, and some q-tips to the watch on arrival. The refurbishing on it is okay, but I did still clean off a thin layer of built up grime from the previous owner, especially in some hard to reach spots.4.) If you are fairly active I recommend getting a different band for the watch. The OEM rubber one ends up slipping all over anytime I build up a sweat. If I try to tighten it enough to stay still, it ends up pinching and cutting off blood flow. I work in food service, so having to constantly readjust the position through my shift has been annoying. I also have slim wrists, and forums seem to say the "no gap" bands are to be avoided. You want that gap so the band can bend down from the mounting point to provide more wrist contact.In summary: This watch has been a super enjoyable addition to my health tracking, Samsung ecosystem, and just general gadgets I use on the daily. I love it! Still giving it 5 stars despite the effort I've had to put in to make everything work right for me, because the price is an absolute steal. I don't have money for a brand new smart watch, but this one still holds its own with the current market, from what I've gathered, and even provides better battery life than a lot of brand new watches.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I want to address two aspects of this purchase: 1) the product itself; and 2) the quality of the refurbished product.Starting with the second, I'm overall very happy with the refurbished quality. There are some obvious signs of wear, but it is on the underside, not visible while wearing. I can't comment on the waterproofing, as I'm not willing to test it out. While I expect there to be a certain amount of water resistance, I do not expect it to be fully waterproof. Functionally, it seems perfect. It was fully reset to factory settings - no old data. The battery life seems good. It lasts me around 3 days, which falls right into the average for this watch. For the price, this has been an excellent value.Concerning the quality of the watch itself, without regard to new or used status, there are some pros and cons. The cons have to do with compatibility with non-Samsung products. The product description makes it seem as if it will be fully compatible with all Android-based phones. This is simply not the case. I have the watch paired with a 2023 Motorola Edge. Firstly, there are some health features, such as the ECG, which are only available when paired with a Samsung device. Also, the watch's Weather app is not compatible with any weather app I've been able to download for my phone. Additionally, I am unable to add watch faces from the Galaxy Wearable app on my phone. However, they may be downloaded and installed directly from the Google App Store with no problem. The issues are mainly due to the differences in how the Galaxy and Motorola products communicate with one another. I had to spend a lot of time messing with permissions, location information, and other privacy and security settings - on both my phone and the watch - in order for it to basically work the way it's supposed to. For weather services, I simply downloaded another app - Weather XL - which works with both the phone and the watch. However, I don't think it will work with watch faces that display weather - I'm still trying to test that out. But ultimately, now that I have it set up it works well and is easy to use. There is definitely a learning curve here, but if you're willing and able to take the time to delve into the various features of the watch and the accompanying phone app, there are some very nice features. I only wish that the description would have noted the possible incompatibilities with non-Samsung products. For the price I paid for the refurbished product, this would not have deterred me from the purchase, but if I had paid the full retail price, I would have been a little upset.Overall, I think this is a very good watch. It looks good, fits well - neither too big nor too small - and contains most of the features I'd want in a watch.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Stay away from Renewed Apple watches!Stay away from Renewed Apple watches!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Be careful purchasing renewed Apple watches. Per Amazon refurbished for Excellent condition:Body: No signs of cosmetic damage (scratches, dents, and other) are visible when the product is held 12 inches away.Battery: When included, batteries have a capacity that exceeds 80% of the original battery life.The first watch I purchased, needed battery servicing. It was under excellent condition of 80% of original battery life. I sent it back and got a different excellent condition watch. It too had the same problems. So I returned that and got a 3rd watch. The scratches weren't as bad, but the battery capacity was still under 80% so I was going to return it but I didn't want to have to deal with a 4th bad watch. So I held onto to it and decided I would keep it. Then 5 days after the return expired, the watch, which is supposed to be able to handle some water, failed to. The watch was used in the shower!! The shower!! The water seal on this refurbished watch failed.So there you have it. $140 for a refurbished watch that lasted 95 days.1. Make sure your watch meets the specifications.2. Do not use this around water, no shower, no pool, etc.

It was essentially useless.EDIT: I now understand the price… the watch itself is in great condition, the watch battery however…. Is not. Under 80% life is just a bit ridiculous. These are refurbished, the seller could have installed a new battery, and I’m sure most buyers would spend the extra $25 to have a fresh battery. The battery in the watch I received doesn’t even last a full day, I have to use my series 3 at night to track sleep… and even that battery lasts longer, it’s 4 years older, and still has 93% batter health. The anxiety that comes with buying refurbished electronics is all too real. The Apple Watch I purchased from this seller came looking brand new, it even came with an Apple approved charging cable (usb-c to lightning), but you will need your own power brick (usb-c output). Very happy with the purchase.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Cheaper than new FOR A GOOD REASON
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Needed a newer Apple Watch so I can do ecgs to share with my doctor. I didn’t want to shell out a shirt load of money for a new one. Saw these renewed ones for a fraction of the price. I ordered one and 2 days later, it showed up. It was in a plain box and had a charger with it. Good thing because it was dead as I’ve ever seen anything dead. It charged up in an hour or so I could get it set up.I inspected it. There are wear marks on the case and crown but the face was fine. I put a screen and case protector on it and it looks fine.I checked the battery life and it’s down to 85%. I’m sure that’s going to be fine. I know it can be replaced it I want to later.The sports band is not an Apple product but I don’t care. I quit buying Apple Watch bands years ago. I can buy 3 or 4 of these perfectly fine knockoffs for the price of one Apple.Other than the scuffs and battery it works as it should.Down with overpriced stuff and thumbs up for cheaper rebuilt semi quality stuff. Kinda like a rebuilt transmission.*****UPDATE*****As for the functionality of the watch, it's fine except for the battery life.  I have to charge it part way through the day IF I want it to last all day.  On more than one occasion, by 4:00 pm, I got the 10% battery left message and then it is dead until I get it on a charger.  Now, I'm going to have to spend $100 to get the battery replaced.AND - the watch charger that came with it, does not work.  Yes, I took the piece of plastic off of it before trying it out.  I'm beginning to regret my purchase.I guess I could see if I can replace the battery myself but I don't want to perform surgery on a piece of electronics at my age.  The battery will be around $25 and the tool kit will be around $30 plus shipping and handling.  Still saving money though.  Maybe I can start a side hustle replacing apple watch batteries and save enough to go on vacation in the tropics or buy a small can of pineapple juice.Buyers remorse is setting in. REMOVE A STAR!*****UPDATE #2*****Found a video tutorial that walked me through turning off a number of the functions of the watch to save on battery.  I am pleased to report that after doing that, I can now wear it 10 or 11 hours and the watch will still have mid 70's battery left.  I shouldn't have to do this but I did so Now I can wear it and not worry about taking a charger to work with me so I can charge it over my lunch break.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: A pesar de haber comprado productos renovados en el pasado, esta fue la primera vez que compré un Apple Watch. Después de leer las experiencias de otros usuarios, donde había opiniones tanto positivas como negativas, decidí probarlo y quedé gratamente sorprendido.El reloj llegó empacado en una caja similar a la de la foto. Aunque no era original, estaba bien empaquetado y venía con un cargador genérico y una correa nueva también genérica.Lo más importante era el reloj en sí. Tenía una estética de un 95%, se notaba que había sido usado porque había un leve desgaste en el sensor óptico, pero la carátula y todo lo demás estaban prácticamente perfectos.La batería tenía un 90% de su capacidad. No tenía bloqueo de iCloud y una vez cargada la batería, pude sincronizarlo con mi iPhone sin ningún problema.Al sincronizarlo, verifiqué los siguientes aspectos:- Estado de salud de la batería.- Funcionamiento de la bocina.- Funcionamiento del micrófono.- Sensibilidad del touch de la pantalla.- Funcionamiento de los botones.Estoy muy contento con mi compra, ya que es un excelente smartwatch a una fracción del precio de uno nuevo. Lo recomiendo totalmente.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: BUYER BEWARE.I purchased a refurbished Apple Watch 8 in excellent condition.  The watch arrived with a scratch on the screen and a cheap knockoff wrist band that was hard to get fitted onto the watch. I was willing to let that go.  I set up the watch.  Charged it and took it off charger around 10pm and went to bed.  I woke up the next morning at 8 am and put on the watch which had already went down to 88% battery life.  By 4pm it was down to 42%.  By this time I’m frustrated so I pull up the source code for the Apple Watch to find out how many battery cycles this watch has been though and the count was 409.As we all know batteries have finite lives.  They can only handle being drained and charged so many times then they need to be replaced.An Apple Watch that has been drained and charged 409 times does not fit the bill of a refurbished item to me.  Not by a long shot and Apple should be ashamed of themselves for letting this take place via an Amazon store with Apple in the name.Do yourself a favor and use my misfortune to come to the right decision

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Charging cable has USB C end.  You may need a USB C female to USB male adapterCharging cable has USB C end.  You may need a USB C female to USB male adapter
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update a few months later.  I returned the watch after writing the previous review; no problems, so the vendor was fine.  I purchased a new watch a non-Apple store.  I had the same problem charging the new one.  It simply would not charge with the charger that came in the new box, so the refurbished watch was probably as good as new.  I purchased a travel charger at Amazon, https://www.amazon.com/NEWDERY-Cordless-Portable-Wireless-Magnetic/dp/B07ZFVYNRQ/ref=sr_1_24?crid=TEHVWGXQ16MK&keywords=apple%2Bwatch%2Bcharger&qid=1684866703&sprefix=apple%2Bwat%2Caps%2C328&sr=8-24&th=1 and it works most of the time.  I've gone from outlet to outlet trying to get the watch to charge.  It's finally found a home in a lower bedroom socket with a USB C adapter.In general, the Apple watch is fairly convenenient for catching calls when the phone is in another room.  There are lots of great watchbands available from 3rd-party vendors for a fraction of what the manufacturer charges for bands.  I like that I have my own photos circulating on it.  It does some weird things, like when I start my car it often tells me how long it will take to get somewhere random, or if not home, how long it will take to get home and what the traffic it like on the highway near home; not on the freeway I need to take to get to that highway.All-in-all, the watch is ok.  There are still times when I put it on the charger at night and it's dead when I take it off the next day.  The Apple-provided charger doesn't work at all. Not really impressed.Update to last week's review:  I received the USB adapter, charged the watch overnight and it didn't start. Put it on a different outlet to charge.  Didn't start.  Held both buttons down for over 10 seconds as recommended by support video.  Never saw the apple or anything else, just a black screen. Returning watch as it was DOA.I'll update the review numbers later.  Just received the watch.  I looks like new and came a few days earlier than expected.  However, I won't know whether it works or not for another week as the charging cable has a USB C end rather than a regular USB end.  My Apple chargers and other USB chargers require the appx. 1/2" rectangular USB end to go into the charger and the C end goes into the device.  I had to order a USB C female to USB male adapter to charge the watch, and it's supposed to arrive in six days.  It actually says "USB C charger" in the write up, so I can't fault the seller. I just hadn't put it together that the C was the part that went into the charger; rather than the watch. I wanted to warn others to order an adapter; if you don't have one; when ordering the watch so you won't be disappointed having to wait for both the watch and then the adapter.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Title: Refreshed Performance: Why the Refurbished Apple Watch Ultra 1 Is a Smart Buy

After setup, performance was snappy: apps launch quickly, GPS locks fast, and fitness tracking (heart rate, workouts, and altitude) matched expectations against my phone’s readings. Battery life held up well through a full day of mixed use including workouts and GPS, and the charging cycle felt consistent with my experience on new units.Buying refurbished brought clear value: I got the core Ultra experience—accurate sensors, excellent durability, and a great display—while saving significantly compared to a brand-new model. The unit I received looked cosmetically clean with minor, unobtrusive wear, and came with a thorough diagnostic check and a reliable warranty from the seller, which gave me extra peace of mind.If you want to save on premium tech, look for seller-provided warranty details and return policies, and verify that the battery health is documented. To score future discounts, subscribe to the seller’s newsletter, follow their social media for flash sales, and check for loyalty or trade-in programs—many vendors offer special codes or trade-in credits that make upgrading even more affordable.A refurbished Apple Watch Ultra 1 is a smart, cost-effective choice for anyone who wants top-tier outdoor and fitness features without the full new-model price tag. Highly recommended.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: (BUY AT YOUR OWN RISK)(BUY AT YOUR OWN RISK)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Let me first state the bad experience I dealt with this watch. When I first received this watch came with some random “smart watch” box doesn’t come with the original Apple box, it also comes with 2 cheap unofficial Apple products which is a charger and wrist band. I’ve heard in the reviews the chargers don’t charge properly with this Apple Watch and it’s true it doesn’t and the band breaks easily, luckily I had an actual solid charger to charge this watch since it also came straight up dead no charge at all, so I was like “okay no big deal” just let it charge for a few mins Apple Watches should always charge quick as they say. 5 mins passes by the watch finally turns on and I was looking to pair it with my phone, it was going well until it was time to  update and I left it there so it can update there was like 2 updates to this Apple Watch so i let the first update go, and it just kept repeating and repeating like it was not updating so I had to literally stay on my watch and see it update but it took SOO LONG it was pissing me off until it finally did the first update now the second update required my phone to stay at least 50% charge or it can stay on the charger while it update. So I did that, I let my watch sit on the charge and it kept telling me AGAIN to make sure my watch is at least on 50% charge or stay on the charger while updating but none of that worked at all meaning my watch was on the charger and it still kept telling me to keep it charged if it’s not at least 50%, so I left it there for at least 20 minutes. 20 minutes passes by and it’s barely 20%!!! I was already looking to refunding this watch already and while it was charging I was looking at reviews having the same issue. Finally 1 hour and 20 minutes it’s 50% and the second update started thank goodness, when everything was done I finally paired it to my phone but battery was not good at all so I was still thinking on refunding this watch since I had to spend more on battery change.But what can I say the watch was smooth, screen and edges were clean clean no damage but my issue was just the battery but I had faith in this watch so I just kept it. After a week of wearing this watch, the battery slowly started getting solid, it charges quicker now first time I charged it yes it did heat up a lot but it’s normal after all the updates it received and to this day no it doesn’t heat that much no more in fact after charging it all night the next morning my watch is on 100% cool not heated up and lasts longer. After a 12 hour shift the battery still is holding at 80% I was shocked at the performance and the watch itself is just beautiful, Siri worked, my calls went through. Though this is still a risk on buying since not everybody has the same performance, I’m guessing my watch was just not updated and turned on for a while that i received a bad experience the first time I got it. I’d say stay patience and see it slowly work.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Review for Apple Watch Ultra 2 (renewed)Review for Apple Watch Ultra 2 (renewed)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was initially hesitant about purchasing a renewed version of the Apple Watch Ultra 2. I wasn’t sure if the “expertly refurbished” label would live up to the standards I expect from Apple products. However, after using it extensively for a week, I’m glad to say that my concerns subsided. Here’s what I’ve liked so far, along with a few areas where there’s room for improvement.Likes:Impressive Performance: Despite being a renewed product, the Apple Watch Ultra 2 performs flawlessly. It's fast, responsive, and handles multitasking like a champ. Whether I’m switching between apps, tracking a workout, or using it for notifications, it’s smooth sailing.Fitness Tracking: This watchOS has completely changed how I track my fitness. The precision of the heart rate monitor, GPS, and various workout modes ensures I’m getting accurate data, which has helped me optimize my training.Health Features: The health tracking features are top-notch. The ECG, and sleep tracking are incredibly insightful, helping me stay on top of my health metrics.Battery Life: I’m pleasantly surprised by the battery life. It easily lasts a couple of days of heavy use, and with lighter use, I can stretch it to almost 2-3 days before needing a charge. Had the Apple Watch series 7 before and it barely lasted a full day.Seamless Integration with Other Devices: As someone who uses multiple Apple products, the Apple Watch Ultra 2 integrates seamlessly with my iPhone, AirPods, and MacBook.Dislikes:Renewed Product Hesitancy: While the renewed version has performed well, there’s still a bit of anxiety in the back of my mind about long-term durability. However, the watch came in excellent condition with no visible wear and tear, so I’m cautiously optimistic.Screen Responsiveness: One major drawback I’ve noticed is that the screen becomes less responsive when my fingers are sweaty during running. This can be frustrating when trying to interact with the watch during a run. I hope this is something that can be improved with software updates, but it’s a noticeable inconvenience.Battery Life: Both a like and a dislike: While the Apple Watch Ultra 2 has more battery life than my recent Apple Watch, it pales in comparison to competitors like Garmin, which can last up to two weeks on a single charge.Overall: I’m incredibly satisfied with my purchase. The Apple Watch Ultra 2 (Renewed) has exceeded my expectations, and I’m confident it will continue to serve me well in my fitness, health, and everyday tech needs. If you’re on the fence about a renewed product, this one is definitely worth considering.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Amazon reviewI've never owned a smart watch because I'm really hard on watches and I just thought they were expensive, fragile gadgets. When my wife got one for health reasons, I saw how useful the watch was and how many ways I could use it.I started looking on Amazon, found the refurbished watches on Woot (Amazon) , found a good price on an Ultra 2 gps+cellular and ordered one. I really love this watch. I love the bigger face, longer battery life and extra features. As stated in the description, the watch was in excellent condition.After it arrived, I wore it a couple of days to make sure it was what I wanted and that it felt good on my wrist. I liked wearing the watch. I ordered a watch face protector because of my bad luck of banging my watches into every hard object I get near. The protector fits great and isn't noticeable on the watch. I also ordered a heavier duty watch band so I wouldn't lose it  during hikes and bike rides.I use it for monitoring my health and tracking my sleep and exercise routine. It is easy to start and finish any type of exercise you know of and many you don't. Knowing how much exercise I'm actually doing during the day keeps me from sitting in the chair too long. It also makes it fun competing against myself.I put the watch on my cellular service and it works well. I enjoy having access to my phone and many apps without bringing my iPhone.Based on my experience, I definitely recommend the refurb watch. No problems and it came in an excellent, like new condition. I also recommend the Ultra 2 for watch face size, longer battery and low power mode, brighter screen, waterproof depth and ruggedness.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Watch is fine, but don't expect genuine accessories.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First the good. The watch is fine, and was actually in really good shape for being used.  The previous owner must Allah have paid for the two  years of prepaid apple care, because the watch still has a couple months of coverage left.The bad. The strap it came with was not a real apple band. It feels impossibly cheap. Like if I paid $5 for it on Temu I would feel like I overpaid.  The listing doesn't specifically say it comes with the apple band, but it also also  doesn't say it doesn't. The fact that the used capitalized terms with the exact same description that apple uses for their genuine ones feels pretty intentionally misleading. It was also so short it was useless for me.Same desk with the charger. It isn't apple, and it is the cheapest charger you could possibly get. I've logged several charges with usb test equipment, and it never goes above 0.18A, which is 0.9W. The real apple one is 18W, so charging takes literally 20X longer with the charger provided then it would with the one originally sold with the watch.Fortunately I already have a couple genuine apple fast chargers, and I ordered a titanium link bracelet with the watch. But if you factor in the additional $130 it would cost you to buy the band and charger that absolutely should have come with the watch it looks like much less of a deal. I wouldn't have bought this had i known, which is probably why the listing forgets to mention them. That said, the watch itself is fine, in good condition, has 100% battery life and couple months of apple care+. I'm not going to return it, so I went with 3 stars

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great for Fitness Tracking, Sleep Monitoring, and Personalization - A Few Minor Drawbacks
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently purchased the SAMSUNG Galaxy Watch 5 (40mm Bluetooth Smartwatch), and overall, I’m quite impressed. Here are the things I love about it:Intuitive Setup: Getting started was straightforward, from installing apps to connecting and creating accounts. Everything synced seamlessly.Tracking: While my primary goal was to track physical activity, I was pleasantly surprised by its sleep monitoring feature. It not only tracks my sleep patterns but also offers tips to improve consistency, which is incredibly helpful.Personalization: It’s easy to change watch faces or swap out bands, making it adaptable to any style or situation.Automatic Activity Recognition: The watch impressively tracks my activities automatically, even when I forget to set up a workout. Whether I’m walking, rowing, following a workout video, or simply tidying up around the house, it picks up my movements accurately without manual input.Convenient Alarm Syncing: I also love how it syncs with my phone alarm. As autumn settles in here in Illinois, mornings can be dark, and alarms are easy to miss. The watch vibrates along with my phone alarm, making it harder to ignore and ensuring I get up on time.What Could Be Improved:Blood Pressure Tracking: While this isn’t Samsung’s fault, I wish the US allowed blood pressure monitoring on this device. I have another watch from Temu with this feature, and it’s incredibly useful for seeing trends and understanding how different events impact my stress levels. It encourages me to manage stress more effectively rather than compartmentalize it.Battery Life: The battery longevity is a bit disappointing. I primarily use the watch for fitness, sleep tracking, and basic functions like stress measurement. Given my moderate usage, I expected the battery to last longer between charges, but I find myself needing to recharge it at least daily - as frequently as my phone.Final Thoughts: Despite these minor drawbacks, the Galaxy Watch 5 is well worth the investment. It’s reliable, versatile, and convenient, and I believe it will last a long time. I would definitely buy it again.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: CHECK YOUR CHARGING PLATECHECK YOUR CHARGING PLATE
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Came as advertised. It has two defects on the silver casing but nothing major. It came completely dead, which is expected with refurbished devices because I’m pretty sure they change the battery and clear them before you buy it. Listen to me when I say this because I’ve seen people complain about the device or charger not working; MAKE SURE YOU TAKE THE PLASTIC PROTECTIVE COVERINGS OFF OF THE CHARGER PLATE BECAUSE IT WILL NOT CHARGE IF YOU DON’T, OR COULD POSSIBLY MELT THE PLASTIC ON THE NON-MAGNETIC SIDE. I was so ready to return this device because it wouldn’t charge or turn on, I somehow was looking at the charging plate and found out that it was because of the very very very thin invisible plastic on the magnetic plate (and the other side). After I got it charged, it worked and set up/connecting wasn’t an issue. The battery did go down quickly the first time, but I didn’t charge it all the way to 100: I tracked my sleep and heart rate for the first time, and it gave me lots of insights on my sleep that I didn’t know about (I ended up buying another app that goes way more in detail). Overall, I’m content with my purchase.

description: Monitor even more of your health with the Apple Watch Series 6. The pulse oximetry to measure your blood's oxygen levels (SpO2) in just 15 seconds, as well as showing you your VO2 Max (maximum oxygen consumption) score. These indicators can provide early warnings to possible respiratory conditions. They are joined by an optical heart rate monitor and the ability to record your own ECG (electrocardiogram). The Series 6 can even detect and healthy habits, such as hand-washing detection, which displays a 20-second animated countdown as you scrub. Fitness is a large part of staying healthy, and the Apple Watch has a variety of ways to assist you in goals. Activity Rings displays three rings that correspond to movement, exercise, and standing. Stay mobile throughout the day to hit new personal bests as you close the rings. You can also choose from a variety of workouts, such as running, swimming, yoga, cycling, and more; with the watch recording and tracking their specific metrics. Fitness and health metrics can be viewed, customized, and tracked on the Apple Watch's curved watch face that houses an always-on LTPO OLED Retina in direct sunlight you can view the screen with just a glance. As you move, choose from a variety of music, podcasts, and audiobooks to entertain and For added fun, share your activity rings with friends and challenge them to 7-day activity competitions. Throughout the day, the Apple Watch Series 6 keeps you connected with the world around you. When paired with your iPhone, you can make calls and send texts your wrist, surroundings with Maps, buy items with Apple Pay, and use your voice to Siri. Made to last in almost any kind of weather, the Apple Watch Series 6 is water-resistant up to 164'. Use its 32GB of built-in storage for apps, watch faces, music, and more.
features: LEAVE YOUR PHONE IN YOUR POCKET: Apple Watch Series 6 GPS Model lets you call, text, and get directions from your wrist, while leaving your phone in your pocket. It offers multiple connectivity options, including: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and NFC to suit all of your possible needs.

ALWAYS-ON RETINA DISPLAY: You no longer need to raise your wrist or touch the screen to see the time or other information on your watch face, because the display never sleeps. All you need to do is glance to find the time or your workout metrics right there where you want them.

ECG ON YOUR WRIST: With the ECG app, Apple Watch Series 6 is capable of generating an ECG similar to a single-lead electrocardiogram. It’s a momentous achievement for a wearable device that can provide data for doctors and peace of mind for you wherever may be during the day.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Too Many Things WrongToo Many Things Wrong
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Everything seemed to be going well when I got the item. It is in fantastic external condition, but within the first day, I realized that the battery would not hold charge. I inspected it after it happened the second day and found that the battery capacity is significantly degraded, down to almost 70%. This is refurbished, so I definitely don’t expect 100%, but I think it’s reasonable to expect 85% or above. What is the point of having this watch if I can’t even wear it long enough for it to get a read before I have to charge it again? Then, four days after its arrival, the side button started malfunctioning. It kept showing the “emergency services” screen when it was just sitting on the nightstand, constantly. The screen showed that the little side icon for the button was held down, even though the button was not stuck at all. This led me to shut the entire thing down every night so that it wouldn’t accidentally call the police! The two days after that, the screen suddenly went black (full charge) and the device entered an infinite boot loop. Just the Apple logo, black screen, Apple logo… etc. every ten seconds. It will not turn on or off, it will not hard reset or force reset. I’ve watched every video. I chatted with Apple support (where Amazon sent me to solve the issue, strangely), who told me it would cost almost $400 to fix the watch. Why on earth would I do that? This was such a disappointing experience for my first Apple Watch.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very Pleased With My Refurbished Apple Watch
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I wanted to swim with my watch, plus to have all the other monitoring features provided by an Apple watch, but I did NOT want to pay what is, to me, a ridiculous price for one. I opted for a refurbished product and am extremely pleased. It looks and behaves like a brand new watch. I put off writing a review until I'd had it for long enough to feel it would have shown me any faults other buyers might want to know. I haven't found any.I have several different bands. The mesh ones (as other reviews will tell you) tend to get tiny breaks in the links that catch on things, but the bands are inexpensive, so economically replaceable. All the watch faces are fun to try out and change your mind about. The watch interfaces nicely with your phone, so you don't have to try to read tiny little type on your watch (though you can, if you wish). You will find that if you want to answer calls via your watch you'll have to pay your phone provider for the privilege, but you don't have to do that, so can dispense with that cost.All in all, I'm very happy with my refurbished Apple watach

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've had this for a few months with mixed results.  I previously had a Fitbit Charge 5, so I can compare the two.  The Pros:- The heart rate monitor is very good.  I had difficulty getting an accurate reading off my Fitbit, this is much better.- It has a much wider range of workouts and works better with a stationary bike and treadmill, both of which I do frequently.- It automatically detects when you are doing a workout such as a walk and will turn on.The Cons:- The battery life is terrible, it has to be charged every day, otherwise it won't make it through the second day.  Sometimes if I have a very active day, such as all day hiking and fishing, it may not even make all the way through the day.  I could go several days with the FitBit before recharging.- I often drive my truck in mountainous area and as soon as I hit a gravel road the bike workout turns on.  Not sure if there is a way to turn this off.  A day in the mountains will guarantee half a dozen false bike workouts.- I like to use the MyFitnessPal app to track my calorie intake.  It does not seem to adjust the calories burned very well.  For example, one day I was hiking and put in 20k+ steps in rigorous hiking, and it only adjusted my calories burned by about 300 from normal.  Pretty sure it was more than that.Overall, I don't feel the need to return it, but probably wouldn't buy it again.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 ReviewThe product under review is the Samsung Galaxy Watch 7, a smartwatch most commonly used by customers as a fitness tracker, a notification tool, and also a daily productivity aid. The initial feeling towards the gadget was very good as Besides having a very contemporary style, the watch was able to maintain a bright screen and very light weight on the wrist.The menu looked very refined and the user never had to deal seriously with the inconvenient navigation.There are such comporaments on the Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 as a heartometer sleeper step-counter GPSplus message notification, and app integration. Users were able to sync the watch with their smartphones to receive calls, texts, and alerts directly on their wrist. The fitness tracking features were Mainly highlighted, as they provide real-time health data during workouts and daily activity.The overall rating of the product amounts to 4.5 stars out of 5. Reasonably speaking, the quality of the whole here is quite high, as it includes health tracking, communication, and smart features all in one device. Was the product able to meet the performance levels? In fact, it not only met them but also slightly surpassed the expectations in the areas of fitness tracking accuracy and display responsiveness.Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 Besides the fact all these features are wrapped in one polished device, the real benefit is the peace of mind from getting away from the phone so often. The user has the option of relying on the fast performance, precise sensors, and good battery life. However, they would need to keep the charging cable handy as the battery life is limited and also, most of the functionality comes when the phone is in a compatible state.For those people using a fitness tracker and a smartwatch as a part of their everyday life, it will Sure happen that they will want to buy one again. Those who are not into high-tech watches or are used to traditional ones and those with limited functionality might not find it useful.Essentially, the Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 is a perfect companion of a person who is very much into Fitness, a student, or a working person who is looking for a complete health tracking and smart device combination.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: High Risk/High (or, SUPER High?) Reward Purchase
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Amazon Renewed — what a “high risk/high reward” type of purchase. I was debating on buying through the Apple refurbished store, and even with a military discount, taxes, and add in Apple Care, I’m close to the price of the most current gen (Ultra 3) in price. The renewed watches do not give the option for Apple Care, though some may come with it already on it (mine did not), look at the warranty program through Amazon—365 DAYS! You’re getting that through the purchase of the watch at no extra cost. For the best purchase experience I’d scroll to the bottom of the item purchase screen and see who the seller/shipper is. I went through Amazon as the seller and shipper so I could go through them if I wanted to return.Now, the high risk/high reward. With taxes I paid less than half the price of an ultra 3. However, even going with the “Premium” renewed line, you never know what is going to come in the box. But with the 365 return period it would definitely be worth the risk. It comes with a third party charger and a lot of the times the battery as dead—WOOIE I can’t believe people complain about this. I already had the charger so it was not a concern of mine. The excitement of getting it delivered was a little unhealthy, I really didn’t know if there’d be scratches/scuffs, or what the battery health of the device would be at.I receive the package, open it up, the body of the device is near PERFECT! Okay, check 1. Next was the most important check. This would determine if I would keep it or send it back, or if I would be able to have this for 6 years like my Series 5 watch. I pair it (you must have an iPhone for the Ultras), charge it, and nervously go to view the battery health….99%!!!! This is a near brand new device that cost me half the price.Doesn’t this sound like a high risk/high reward?  If you’re in the market, go here and get the “Premium” condition and follow the steps I laid out. You may get a beater, but hey, return it and try again and save yourself several hundred dollars. Buy a ESR screen protector that protects the plateau where the screen is. I can’t even tell I have one on. These watches last for days on a single charge, have a massive screen (49 MM) and can look extremely classy, athletic, or even chill with the multiple band types.If this helps and you’re leaning towards yes, do it. Take the risk like you would a card pack and see what you get. You may pull yourself a holo Charizard!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Sleek, Feature-Packed Smartwatch, but Renewed Unit Needs Extra Care
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased the Google Pixel Watch 2 (Matte Black Aluminum, Obsidian Active Band, GPS, Renewed) about three weeks ago to track my fitness, monitor stress, and stay connected during family activities with my 10- and 11-year-old nephew and son, like Wii gaming with our Eanetf sensor bar or walks in the park. As someone who values practical, tech-savvy solutions (think SMARTTOP nose pads and HOOBRO bathroom shelf), I wanted an Android smartwatch with Fitbit integration at a budget-friendly price. After using it for 15-18 days, here’s my detailed take on its performance, including pros, cons, and tips for other buyers, especially those considering a renewed unit.How I Used ItThis Pixel Watch 2 (41mm, Wi-Fi/GPS, renewed) features a 1.2” AMOLED display (450x450, 1000 nits), 100% recycled aluminum case, Wear OS 4, and Fitbit integration for heart rate, stress, sleep, and ECG tracking, plus safety features like Fall Detection and Emergency SOS. It includes three new sensors (heart rate, skin temperature, cEDA for stress), a 306mAh battery (24-hour rated), and a 6-month Fitbit Premium trial. I paired it with my Google Pixel 7 (Android 14) for notifications, calls, and Google apps (Maps, Calendar, Assistant), using GPS for 3-4 outdoor walks (2-3 miles each) and Auto Workout for indoor treadmill runs (30 minutes at 6 mph). I tracked sleep 10 nights, stress during work, and heart rate daily, charging it every 24-28 hours with the included USB-C cable. I cleaned the renewed watch with alcohol wipes, replaced the band due to wear, and stored it near my TheraBreath rinse in our bathroom.ProsAccurate Health Tracking: The Fitbit heart rate sensor, enhanced by Google AI, is spot-on during walks and runs, matching my chest strap within 2-3 BPM, as praised on Google’s Store for its precision. Sleep tracking detailed light, deep, and REM stages, helping me adjust bedtime.Effective Stress Management: The cEDA sensor’s Body Response feature alerted me to stress during work calls, prompting breathing exercises via Fitbit, which I found calming, as noted in a @madebygoogle post. Skin temperature tracking also hinted at sleep environment tweaks.Seamless Google Integration: Pairing with my Pixel 7 was a breeze, with notifications (Gmail, Calendar) and Google Assistant responding smoothly, as Amazon reviewers lauded for Android users. I answered calls and used Maps for navigation on walks.Sleek, Comfortable Design: The 41mm matte black case and obsidian band look stylish and feel light (31g), perfect for all-day wear, even with my Gildan boxer briefs and FIONECA shorts, as Best Buy reviewers noted for comfort. The AMOLED display is vibrant at 1000 nits.Great Renewed Value: At $120-$150, it’s a steal compared to $350 new, arriving in excellent condition (minor band wear), with a new charger and 6-month Fitbit Premium, as an Amazon reviewer praised for renewed deals.ConsRenewed Unit Cleanliness: The watch had dirt in the crown and band connectors, requiring 15 minutes of cleaning with alcohol wipes and a toothpick, echoing Amazon reviews about inconsistent renewed quality. The band was slightly worn, so I bought a BandRain nylon band ($15).Battery Life Limitations: The 306mAh battery lasts 24-28 hours with light use (no GPS), but GPS walks drained it to 20% in 2 hours, needing daily charging, as Amazon reviewers noted (104 negative vs. 52 positive). A 75-minute charge restores it fully.Small Size for Larger Wrists: The 41mm case and band felt snug on my 7.5-inch wrist, with only 1-2 holes left, as Amazon reviewers mentioned for small wrists. The crown pressed into my wrist when bending, so a larger band helped.Adhesive Residue on Band: The renewed band had sticky residue, making it uncomfortable until replaced, similar to an Amazon review about band quality issues. A quick swap fixed it, but it’s an extra step for renewed buyers.ComparisonsCompared to the Fitbit Versa 4 ($200), the Pixel Watch 2 offers better Google app integration and safety features (Emergency SOS, Fall Detection) but shorter battery life, per Amazon. The Google Pixel Watch 1 ($100 renewed) lacks the cEDA and temperature sensors, making the 2 a worthwhile upgrade, per Google Store. My SMARTTOP nose pads improved glasses comfort, but this watch’s health insights are more impactful than the HOOBRO shelf’s storage. The Samsung Galaxy Watch 5 ($180 renewed) has longer battery life (40 hours) but less seamless Pixel phone syncing, per Amazon. The Pixel Watch 3 ($350 new) adds running insights but isn’t worth the premium for my needs, per Best Buy. This renewed Pixel Watch 2 balances features and price for Android users.Tips for BuyersClean Renewed Units Thoroughly: Use alcohol wipes and a toothpick to clean dirt from the crown and band connectors, as Amazon reviews suggest for renewed watches. Check band condition and consider a $15 nylon replacement for comfort.Manage Battery Life: Charge daily (75 minutes for full) and disable always-on display or GPS for lighter use to stretch to 28 hours, addressing Amazon’s battery complaints. A 10-minute top-up adds 4-5 hours.Size Up Bands for Larger Wrists: If your wrist is over 7 inches, get a BandRain Stretchy Nylon Band ($15) for a better fit, as Amazon reviewers noted for small bands. Adjust the crown to avoid wrist pressure.Test Safety Features: Set up Emergency SOS and Safety Check with trusted contacts via the Fitbit app, testing Fall Detection in a safe setting, per Google’s instructions. Ensure Wi-Fi/GPS is active for location sharing.Who Should Buy This?The Google Pixel Watch 2 (Matte Black, GPS, Renewed) is ideal for Android users (Pixel/Samsung phones) needing accurate heart rate, stress, and sleep tracking with Google app integration and safety features for walks or daily use. It’s a great value for budget-conscious buyers but requires cleaning and band checks for renewed units. For longer battery life, consider the Galaxy Watch 5, per Amazon.Overall, this Pixel Watch 2 has been a fantastic addition, offering precise health insights and seamless connectivity for my active lifestyle. It’s stylish and functional, though renewed units need extra TLC and daily charging. I’m eyeing a metal mesh band next for a dressier look! If you’ve tried this or have smartwatch tips, share in the comments—I’d love to hear your thoughts!

It also has a label saying not to use a fast charger and that only a 5W charger should be used. Unfortunately, a compatible 5W USB-C charger is not included, which makes charging a little inconvenient.Another downside is the shipping time. It took almost a month from placing the order to receiving the watch, which was much longer than I expected.Overall, it's a decent value if you can accept some normal wear, but I don't think the condition truly matches the "Excellent" description.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I recently upgraded from a 45mm Series 9 to the new Black Titanium Apple Watch Ultra 3. Instead of paying the $799 retail price, I decided to take a gamble on an "Open Box" unit from iPower Resale for $609. The gamble paid off flawlessly. The watch arrived in its original box, and the included charger and watch band were still sealed in Apple's factory packaging. Checking the settings, the battery health is sitting dead-on at exactly 100%, and the device still has an active Apple Limited Warranty until January 2027. For all intents and purposes, I saved $190 on a brand-new watch.Size & The Screen UpgradeA lot of the online consensus claims that jumping from a 45mm Series watch to the 49mm Ultra isn't that noticeable of a screen difference. I completely disagree. The switch to the flat sapphire crystal glass changes the entire experience. Because it doesn't curve off at the edges like the Series 9, the usable screen real estate feels massive. Add in the 3,000 nits of brightness, and the display is incredibly crisp and visible from across the room.Comfort & Battery LifeIs the watch huge? Yes, it is objectively a large, thick piece of titanium. But despite the visual bulk, it is surprisingly balanced on the wrist. It doesn't feel like you are wearing a brick, and it is comfortable enough that I sleep in it every single night without any discomfort.The biggest quality-of-life improvement coming from the Series 9 is the battery. Being able to track sleep all night and wake up without needing a "panic charge" to get through the workday is a game-changer.The Verdict: 5/5 StarsIf you are on the fence about the 49mm size, it is worth the jump. The Black Titanium finish looks incredibly premium, the flat screen is a massive functional upgrade, and if you can find a verifiable mint open-box deal with the factory warranty intact, it is an absolute steal.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Love it! Much better than I expected, Refurbished but like brand new
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was a little reluctant to try and save some money by getting a refurbished Apple watch, some of the reviews sounded like they quality on the refurb was a bit spotty, so I was expecting to get something that looked used but I was totally blown away by what I actually received.  The first thing was the shipping speed, UNBELIEVABLE!!! I ordered this at 3PM in the afternoon and it was delivered before 1PM the following day and it shipped from halfway across the country. What I received was a generic box with a well wrapped, like new apple watch series 6 and a an unused OEM packaged apple watch charger. The watch looks like new, it was simple to set up and it works great! upping from a series 3 I love the larger 44mm display, the always on display and the new watch faces but  can only give it a mediocre score on battery life, I put it on the charger next to my bed every night and its fully charged every morning when I put it on, but at the end of the night the battery is down to 50%, so I don;t bother with the sleep tacking bit, because then it wouldn't be ready to wear for a full days use the next day. I haven't tried the advance monitoring features but its nice to know they are there. I did put a metal band on it and it makes a world of difference with the comfort and wearability it feels very satisfying on the wrist. . I was considering the SE and changed my mind at the last minute, I think either would have been fine but I do like the always on display, one of the things that bugged me about the series 3 is  the display did not stay on long enough sometimes and it was frustrating to tap and roll your wrist repeatedly trying to get the display came back on, but this series 6 doesn't have that problem. All in, I'm happy with my purchase and  if I could go back, I wouldn't change anything.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: reliable and consistent despite mediocre battery life
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: update: after a few days of use, I have noticed the battery lasts just about a day. But since I am alternating with the other watch, it is not that big a deal for me. Also, the sleep tracking does seem to be more accurate than the series 4, so that is something I will be using this watch to monitor. I also like to use the "always on" display at work where I look at my watch often.I have a series 4 that has been my main watch for a while, now. It does most of what I need it to do, and it is reliable in the things it does well. But the battery life is not great, as you probably already know. I wanted a backup to wear while I charge it. I tried a cheaper alternative, but I have grown accustomed to certain features, so I got this series 6 to use alternately with my series 4. The "always on" display option might be helpful at work where I look at my watch often.when I synced to my phone, it gave me the option to use my current watch settings, so I did that, which was very convenient. However, both watches have the same name, now, which is less convenient. Not a deal breaker, however.It is disappointing that the spo2 has been disabled by apple. But again, not a deal breaker for me. I am more concerned about the heart rate monitoring, which works pretty well for my purposes. I will try the sleep monitoring, as well, to see if I find it useful.there are plenty of useful watch faces and I like that they can be customized to some extent. I have one for work, and a few others for personal use.I haven't used many other smart watches other than a fitbit, which became glitchy, especially in reading my heart rate. The apple watches have been reliable and work well with my iphone. So I decided to stick with what works for me.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: UpdateI bought this 8/14/2022.It’s 10/4/2025 now.Protected by the same 6-pack of snap-on protectors, the capabilities far outweigh the inconvenience of keeping a device on my wrist. I used to not wear a watch at all, for lack of utility, and lack of comfort.Elastic fabric bands, and cheap snap-on protectors have provided much more protection and convenience than their cost.The battery still gets me through a whole day, and charges in an evening between returning from work and going to bed.Apple needs to come out with something spectacularly better for me to care about upgrading.===Firstly, I’ve never liked wearing a watch, especially because I don’t like most bands available. So this was a big leap of faith.As for value, $260 (at time of purchase) seems reasonable for a backup cellular device like this.QualityThere’s a 1x3mm scuff right beside one of the band-slots, but no functionality is hindered, and a case covers it.-no other negative quality issues are noticed (yet).On function-It gives me volume control on my AirPods Pro through, which is the only feature AirPods Pro are lacking in built-in features.-I’m able to get important info without spending time on my phone’s screen (reducing overall usage of screens in a day).-the alarm sounds are well-thought, and the vibration feels like someone is sweetly grabbing my wrist and gently wiggling it to wake me up. On that note, even for me, the watch (and the bands I bought in addition to the stock band) is comfortable enough to sleep in.-watch faces aren’t as diverse and artistic as I hoped, but they’re still decent. I have one that shows me the sun’s relative position in the sky on a time-scale of the day (one of the Solar Dial faces), which makes me think differently about chronologically when I am in my waking hours.Other thoughts-If you’re going to use it for a phone call, don’t lift your elbow high like an antenna to listen on the same side. Cross over your chest and use the opposite ear like a proper Starfleet cadet.-I’m not a wristwatch kind of person, neither am I particularly fashionable. But this is comfy, and the availability of 3rd party cases and bands make it easy to add an essence of expression to your daily demeanor.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this pretty quickly and it (and the renewed iphone xr I bought at the same time) are my very first apple products. You can't tell it's renewed at all. I saw no signs of any scuffs, scratches or anything! Performance is excellent.I come from using a Samsung Active 2 and there are SO MANY more apps. Apps that they both have work better too. For example on my samsung, I could only respond to a facebook message if someone sent me a message. On the Apple Watch 6 I can find the app on the list and view all the messages, even pictures! I love that you can handwrite responses. Voice input is better as well.ECG: I have atrial fibrillation, so that was my biggest reason for buying the watch. I bought the Samsung Active 2 because I suspected heart issues but we could never catch them. The ECG on Samsung worked only when you put your finger on it. It often was really picky about the pressure you put on it resulting in lots of reading errors and artifacts. I switched to Apple because many other afib people said it can detect and alert you to an episode. I haven't had an alert yet but I think my afib is under control at the moment. Still, it gives much cleaner ECGs with almost no artifacts. Doesn't do the crazy up and downs that Samsung did if you didn't keep the pressure perfect when taking a measurement.The amount of health data that can be tracked is unreal. I was able to link my patient charts from my doctors which shows and takes into account health data. I have continuous glucose monitoring and log my readings in it also. It even links up with my pokemon go so much better.I'm super happy with this purchase. I saw it as an investment in my health and I got on top of that so many great additions that I didn't realize I was missing on Android/Samsung. I am now an Apple convert.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I decided to give the renewed version of the Apple Watch SE (2nd Gen) a try, and I'm glad I did. It offers most of the features I wanted from an Apple Watch while saving a significant amount compared to buying new.When the watch arrived, I was pleasantly surprised by its condition. The screen looked great with no noticeable scratches during normal use, and the aluminum case was in excellent shape. If I hadn't known it was renewed, I would have assumed it was new or very lightly used.Setup with my iPhone was quick and straightforward. Within minutes I had notifications, fitness tracking, Apple Pay, and my favorite apps synced and ready to go. The watch feels responsive, and navigating menus is smooth with no lag or performance issues.The 44mm size strikes a nice balance between screen space and comfort. The display is easy to read, whether I'm checking messages, tracking workouts, or glancing at the weather. The Midnight aluminum case and matching sport band also give it a clean, modern look that works well for both casual and professional settings.Battery life has been consistent throughout the day. I typically wear it from morning until bedtime for activity tracking, notifications, and occasional workouts, and I still have battery remaining at the end of the day. Charging overnight has become part of my routine.One of the biggest benefits has been the fitness and health tracking. Activity rings, step counts, heart rate monitoring, and workout tracking provide useful information without being complicated. It has helped me stay more aware of my daily activity levels.Pros:Excellent condition for a renewed productEasy setup and seamless iPhone integrationResponsive performanceComfortable 44mm sizeUseful fitness and activity trackingGreat value compared to buying newCons:Battery health may vary slightly between renewed unitsDoes not include some premium features found on higher-end Apple Watch modelsOverall, the Apple Watch SE (2nd Gen) delivers a great smartwatch experience at a more affordable price point. If you're already in the Apple ecosystem and want reliable notifications, fitness tracking, and everyday convenience, the renewed version is an excellent value and performs much like a new device.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the first Apple Watch I have owned, and I was hesitant about buying a "renewed" watch.  The Apple Watch SE (2nd Gen) purchased as Renewed "Excellent" condition was received in near new condition.  I did not find any visible scratches and the battery health was at 94% level.  It did require charging when received before it could be used.Pairing to my iPhone 15 was as simple as placing the watch next to the iPhone, with Blue tooth enabled, and following on-screen instructions.  The watch did require updating the iOS to 26 before pairing could be completed.  So, don't be in a hurry to use the watch after you receive.  Give it time to update and pair.The watch did come with a new band, and a wireless charger with USB C connector.I have already taken advantage of the many health features of the Apple Watch.  It's been great so far.If I am to dock any points off this purchase, it will be 0.5 pts for the wireless charger.  It seems to be low Wattage as it took about 4 hours or more to first charge the watch.  I was using a power block rated 35 watts, so it wasn't my power supply.I recommend to anyone buying an Apple watch to purchase a screen protector of some type.  I also recommend purchasing a wireless charger with higher output.  I did end up purchasing a 22W 3 in 1 wall charger with built-in magnetic Wireless charger for Apple watches.  The wireless charger is rated 2.5 Watts, and it charges the Apple Watch SE much quicker than the corded charger provided with the watch.
